chunks.heading: First Law of Thermodynamics & Internal Energy
chunks.content: The First Law of Thermodynamics states that the change in internal energy ΔU of a closed system equals the net heat transfer Q into the system minus the net work W done by the system: ΔU = Q - W. Internal energy U is a state function that depends only on the current equilibrium state of the system, not on the path taken to reach that state.

chunks.heading: Second Law of Thermodynamics & Entropy
chunks.content: The Second Law of Thermodynamics establishes that the total entropy S of an isolated system never decreases over time (ΔS >= 0). Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body without external work being performed. For a reversible Carnot heat engine operating between reservoirs TH and TC, maximum thermal efficiency is η_max = 1 - (TC / TH).

chunks.heading: Quadratic Formula & Discriminant Analysis
chunks.content: For any second-degree polynomial equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a != 0, the roots are given by x = (-b ± sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / (2a). The discriminant Δ = b^2 - 4ac determines root nature: Δ > 0 yields two distinct real roots, Δ = 0 yields one repeated real root, and Δ < 0 yields two complex conjugate roots.

chunks.heading: Integration by Parts & Fundamental Theorem
chunks.content: If f is continuous on [a, b] and F is any antiderivative of f such that F'(x) = f(x), then the definite integral from a to b of f(x)dx equals F(b) - F(a). Integration by parts follows from the product rule: ∫ u dv = u v - ∫ v du.
